config_version.description: Format version this firmware accepts. Raise the maximum when the firmware learns a newer layout; the check is generated, so it cannot be forgotten.

device_name.description: Identifies this unit: the mDNS hostname, the MQTT client id, and the substitution for $DEVICE$ in the MQTT topic prefix.

instance_name.description: Human-readable name shown by mDNS browsers

feeder_id.description: Which feeder this device is bolted to. 0 means unprovisioned: the device boots, joins the network and answers the console, but publishes no measurement topics and says so loudly on every status. It is deliberately not a silent fallback -- the predecessor's fallback of 999 produced a device that published to a topic nobody watched.

board.description: How the parts are wired. Pin numbers are a fact about the board, not about any driver, so they live here rather than in a header.

i2c_sda.description: I2C data pin. Every part on this board is on it: the NAU7802 at 0x2A, the SHT4x, and the INA237. -1 disables the bus and with it all three.

i2c_hz.description: I2C bus speed. The NAU7802 is specified to 400 kHz; 100 kHz is the safe default for a sensor on a flying lead.

nau7802_drdy.description: GPIO the NAU7802's DRDY output is wired to, or -1 to poll PU_CTRL.CR over I2C instead. Wire it if you can: polling runs on the FreeRTOS tick, so a result read can land exactly as the device rewrites its registers and stitch one reading out of two conversions. Near zero that is a huge outlier; anywhere else it passes for noise.

sht4x_address.description: 0x44, 0x45 or 0x46 as decimal. The variant fitted decides it; there are no address pins, so the address is a fact about which part was fitted rather than how it was strapped. Note the overlap with the INA237's range: 0x44-0x46 are legal for both parts, and two devices answering one address is a fault the firmware refuses to start on rather than diagnose later.

ina237_address.description: 0x40 to 0x4F as decimal, selected by the A0/A1 pins (Table 7-2), or -1 when no INA237 is fitted. -1 starts nothing and logs nothing: the part is simply not there, which status reports as 'not-fitted' rather than 'failed'.

vin_adc_gpio.description: GPIO an input-voltage divider is wired to, or -1 for none. Must be an ADC-capable pin. Used for bus_v when there is no INA237; with one fitted, the INA237 wins and this is ignored. Voltage only: a divider says nothing about current, so a board measuring this way reports none.

vin_divider_top_ohms.description: The divider resistor between the input voltage and vin_adc_gpio.

vin_divider_bottom_ohms.description: The divider resistor between vin_adc_gpio and ground. The input voltage is the pin voltage times (top + bottom) / bottom. A divider this high-impedance wants a capacitor of 100 nF or more at the pin, or the ADC's sampling charge pulls the reading low.

loadcell.description: The NAU7802 front end and the filter chain on top of it. The defaults reproduce the response of the HX711-based predecessor: an 18-deep trimmed sliding mean inside the amplifier driver, and a 5-deep average of that in the application.

rate_sps.description: Conversion rate: 10, 20, 40, 80 or 320. 10 matches the predecessor exactly, which is what makes its empirically tuned trigger thresholds transferable. One sample costs average_samples conversions of wall time, so the sample rate is rate_sps / average_samples.

gain.description: PGA gain: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 or 128. A load cell bridge at 2 mV/V needs the top of this range; a gain left at 1 puts the signal among the noise while still producing plausible numbers.

internal_ldo.description: Power the bridge from the NAU7802's own regulator. False leaves AVDD taken from the pin, which is the chip default -- switching the regulator on while the board already drives AVDD would put two sources on one net.

calibration_factor.description: Counts per gram, at this gain. Negative is legitimate and inverts the sign for a cell wired the other way round -- do not take the absolute value. A factor measured by 'scale calibrate' is stored in NVS and wins over this one; this is the factory default a device falls back to.

tare_counts.description: The unloaded zero, in raw counts. Persisted in NVS by 'scale tare' and restored at boot, so reported weights are absolute feeder mass rather than a change relative to whenever the device last rebooted. The predecessor re-tared at every boot with the feeder in place, which silently redefined zero on every reset.

tare_on_boot.description: Re-tare at boot with whatever is on the cell, discarding the stored zero. This reproduces the predecessor's behaviour and is almost never what you want: it makes weights incomparable across a reboot and makes syrup consumption unmeasurable.

window_conversions.description: Depth of the sliding window the trimmed mean runs over

trim_high.description: Highest values discarded from each window before averaging

trim_low.description: Lowest values discarded from each window before averaging

average_samples.description: Trimmed-mean outputs averaged into one sample, one per new conversion. Because the window slides, these overlap heavily: one sample is not an independent 90-conversion average, and its settling time is about 22 conversions. A reimplementation that simply averaged 90 conversions would be measurably slower and would miss short landings.

baseline_samples.description: Samples averaged to establish the startup baseline, and to re-establish it after a re-baseline

startup_timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for the converter to produce conversions before declaring a sensor fault. The predecessor called an infinite delay loop here, which reported nothing and never recovered.

trigger.description: Landing detection. These thresholds were tuned empirically against the previous mechanical arrangement; a different cell, mounting or noise floor means re-tuning them against recorded raw_batch data rather than carrying them over.

min_g.description: Below this change from the baseline, not a bird. Against a hummingbird mass of 3-6 g this implies partial weight transfer -- perching while still hovering.

max_g.description: Above this, not a bird: a refill, or the feeder being knocked

hysteresis_g.description: The settled band. The weight must fall back inside it for a trigger to clear, and only inside it does the baseline move.

reset_interval_samples.description: Cap on a single continuous trigger. Once this many samples have elapsed the trigger branch stops re-arming for the rest of the event; the trigger stays asserted and still clears only when the weight settles.

baseline_alpha.description: Weight given to a new settled sample: baseline := (1-alpha)*baseline + alpha*sample. The baseline is frozen on any iteration that is not settled, deliberately, so a feeding bird is never absorbed into it.

average_every.description: Publish the baseline to 'average' on every Nth loop iteration. The counter advances every iteration but the publish only happens on a settled one, so these are irregular and are skipped entirely during activity.

rebaseline_after_s.description: Re-acquire the baseline after this long continuously outside the settled band, clearing any asserted trigger. 0 disables it, which reproduces the predecessor's lockup: a refill freezes the baseline permanently and only a reboot recovers.

telemetry.description: What gets published, how often, and how much of it fits in one message

batch_entries.description: Entries in one published batch. This is the count actually published: the predecessor flushed when the buffer *exceeded* its batch size and so published 257, which is corrected here rather than reproduced.

batch_max_bytes.description: Flush early if the serialised payload would exceed this. The predecessor fixed the count against a 2048-byte buffer and failed intermittently once readings needed a third integer digit; sizing by payload is what makes that impossible rather than merely unlikely. Must stay under the MQTT client's outbound buffer (CONFIG_MQTT_BUFFER_SIZE).

batch_drop_entries.description: Discard the buffer once it holds this many entries, whatever the publish did. Bounds both memory and staleness when the broker is unreachable for a long time.

environment_interval_s.description: How often to read and publish the SHT4x. 0 disables it.

power_interval_s.description: How often to read and publish the input voltage (and, with an INA237, current and power). 0 disables it.

status_interval_s.description: How often to publish the retained status message

debug_echo.description: Mirror every console line to the 'message' topic. Off by default; the publish path guards against re-entry, so a failure inside the echo cannot try to publish about itself.

power.description: The INA237 and the shunt it measures across. Only the shunt is configurable: the driver writes SHUNT_CAL and nothing else, leaving the ADC range and averaging at the reset values the datasheet's own design example prescribes.

shunt_ohms.description: The resistor actually fitted, in ohms. The part measures a voltage across something it knows nothing about, so there is no discoverable default and getting this wrong scales every current and power reading without anything looking amiss.

watchdog.description: Two watchdogs with different jobs: one catches firmware that has stopped running, the other catches firmware that is running and useless.

hardware_s.description: Task watchdog timeout. The sampling task subscribes and feeds it, so a blocked conversion loop resets the device. 0 disables it.

external_ms.description: Countdown reset by any message on the 'watchdog' topic; on reaching zero the device restarts. This is how an external supervisor recovers a device that is connected but not working. 0 disables it.

arm_on_first_message.description: Start the countdown only once a watchdog message has actually arrived, so a device deployed without a supervisor is not rebooted every two minutes by a timer nothing feeds. That is precisely what happened to the predecessor: it counted down from boot and subscribed only to 'control', so the message that would have reset the countdown was never delivered.
